"'''I Don't Wanna Know'''" is a song by American singer [[Mario Winans]], featuring American rapper [[Sean Combs|P. Diddy]] and Irish singer [[Enya]]. The song is based on a sample of the [[Fugees]]' song "[[Ready or Not (Fugees song)|Ready or Not]]", which in turn samples the synthesizer riff from Enya's song "[[Boadicea (song)|Boadicea]]".<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=uw8EAAAAMBAJ&pg=PA64|title=OutKast 'Moves' Past Itself to Claim No. 1|last1=Pietroluongo|first1=Silvio|last2=Patel|first2=Minal|last3=Jessen|first3=Wade|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|volume=116|issue=7|page=64|date=February 14, 2004}}</ref> The drums are sampled from the end of [[EPMD]]'s "You're a Customer", though the writers ([[Erick Sermon]] and [[Parrish Smith]]) were not initially credited.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.vibe.com/features/editorial/erick-sermon-esp-interview-359792/|title=Erick Sermon Talks 'E.S.P.' Album And Hip-Hop Then Versus Now|last=Robertson|first=Darryl|magazine=[[Vibe (magazine)|Vibe]]|date=July 7, 2015|access-date=December 2, 2022}}</ref><ref name="auscd1"/>

Released on February 17, 2004, "I Don't Wanna Know" spent eight consecutive weeks at number two on the US [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]], behind the [[Usher (singer)|Usher]] singles "[[Yeah! (Usher song)|Yeah!]]" and "[[Burn (Usher song)|Burn]]", respectively,<ref>{{cite magazine|url=http://www.billboard.com/charts/hot-100/2004-04-24|title=Billboard Hot 100|magazine=Billboard|date=April 24, 2004|access-date=June 19, 2005}}</ref> and reached number one in Germany, the Netherlands, and the United Kingdom. It became a top-10 hit in many other countries, including Australia, Canada, France, Ireland, and New Zealand, and has received multiple [[Music recording certification|sales certifications]].

In 2022, record producer [[Metro Boomin]], singer [[the Weeknd]], and rapper [[21 Savage]] released the single "[[Creepin' (Metro Boomin, the Weeknd and 21 Savage song)|Creepin']]", a [[cover version|cover]] of the song mainly performed by the Weeknd, with a rap verse performed by 21 Savage instead of P. Diddy. Winans himself contributed to this version, while Diddy himself would be featured on the official remix of the song, released in March 2023.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://radio.callmefred.com/en/song_story/creepin-metro-boomin-the-weeknd-21-savage/|title=The Story of the Song Creepin by Metro Boomin, The Weeknd, 21 Savage|website=radio.callmefred.com|access-date=March 6, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.complex.com/music/metro-boomin-diddy-creepin-remix-the-weeknd-21-savage|title=Diddy Hops on Metro Boomin's 'Creepin' (Remix)' and Music Video f/ The Weeknd and 21 Savage|website=[[Complex Networks|Complex]]|access-date=March 17, 2023}}</ref>

"I Don't Wanna Know" is a song by American singer Mario Winans, featuring American rapper P. Diddy and Irish singer Enya. The song is based on a sample of the Fugees' song "Ready or Not", which in turn samples the synthesizer riff from Enya's song "Boadicea". The drums are sampled from the end of EPMD's "You're a Customer", though the writers (Erick Sermon and Parrish Smith) were not initially credited.

Released on February 17, 2004, "I Don't Wanna Know" spent eight consecutive weeks at number two on the US Billboard Hot 100, behind the Usher singles "Yeah!" and "Burn", respectively, and reached number one in Germany, the Netherlands, and the United Kingdom. It became a top-10 hit in many other countries, including Australia, Canada, France, Ireland, and New Zealand, and has received multiple sales certifications.

In 2022, record producer Metro Boomin, singer the Weeknd, and rapper 21 Savage released the single "Creepin'", a cover of the song mainly performed by the Weeknd, with a rap verse performed by 21 Savage instead of P. Diddy. Winans himself contributed to this version, while Diddy himself would be featured on the official remix of the song, released in March 2023.

sections.heading: Composition
sections.wikitext: The song is sung over a background track that samples "[[Boadicea (song)|Boadicea]]" by [[Enya]] from her 1987 debut album ''Enya'', inspired by the use of the sample in the [[Fugees]]' 1996 hit single "[[Ready or Not (Fugees song)|Ready or Not]]".<ref>{{Cite magazine |title=Billboard: February 14, 2004 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=uw8EAAAAMBAJ&dq=i+dont+wanna+know+mario+fugees&pg=PA64 |magazine=Billboard| date=February 14, 2004 }}</ref> Winans said: "I first heard 'Boadicea' at the end of the movie ''[[Sleepwalkers (1992 film)|Sleepwalkers]]'' about five or six years ago. It's something I always wanted to produce. Then when the Fugees did it, oh my God, I loved it."<ref>{{cite web|title=P.Diddy pays out for Enya sample|url=http://www.hotpress.com/Enya/news/PDiddy-pays-out-for-Enya-sample/2719304.html|website=Hot Press|access-date=August 9, 2016|date=March 29, 2004}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Mario Winans : Love, Hurt, Betrayal: These Are A Few Of Mario Winans' Favorite Things - Rhapsody Music Downloads |url=http://www.vh1.com/artists/news/1485854/03192004/winans_mario.jhtml |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120716183800/http://www.vh1.com/artists/news/1485854/03192004/winans_mario.jhtml |archive-date=July 16, 2012 |access-date=May 20, 2012 |publisher=VH1.com}}</ref>
sections.text: The song is sung over a background track that samples "Boadicea" by Enya from her 1987 debut album Enya, inspired by the use of the sample in the Fugees' 1996 hit single "Ready or Not". Winans said: "I first heard 'Boadicea' at the end of the movie Sleepwalkers about five or six years ago. It's something I always wanted to produce. Then when the Fugees did it, oh my God, I loved it."

sections.heading: Critical reception
sections.wikitext: ''[[Vibe (magazine)|Vibe]]'' wrote that "Winans adds a simple stuttering beat that prevents the song from devolving into murky, saccharine Muzak. This is the secret of Winan's magic; the soft touch of the synthesizers and his gentle piano playing blend with the signature sound of the kick and snare – hard, unadorned, punching through the music's gauzy [[elegy|elegiac]] texture."<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=siYEAAAAMBAJ&q=i+don%27t+wanna+know&pg=PA151|title=Mario Winans – Hurt No More|last1=Ehrlich|first1=Dimitri|magazine=Vibe|page=152|date=June 2004|access-date=August 9, 2016}}</ref>

sections.heading: Commercial performance
sections.wikitext: "I Don't Wanna Know" peaked at number two on the US [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] for eight weeks and reached the same position on the [[Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Singles & Tracks]] chart.<ref name="hot100"/><ref name="usrandb"/> It topped the ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' [[Rhythmic (chart)|Rhythmic]] chart and also peaked at number four on the [[Mainstream Top 40]] ranking.<ref name="usr"/><ref name="usps"/> The song was a radio hit in Canada, reaching number two on ''[[Radio & Records]]''{{'}} CHR/Pop Top 30 chart.<ref name="can"/> Outside North America, the song reached number one on the [[Eurochart Hot 100]],<ref name="eur"/> topping the charts of Germany, the Netherlands, and the United Kingdom.<ref name="ger"/><ref name="d40"/><ref name="uk"/> Across the rest of Europe, the song became a top-five hit in several regions, including [[Flanders]], France, Ireland, Norway, and Switzerland.<ref name="fla"/><ref name="ire"/> In [[Australasia]], "I Don't Wanna Know" peaked at number two in Australia and number three in New Zealand.<ref name="aus"/><ref name="nz"/>
sections.text: "I Don't Wanna Know" peaked at number two on the US Billboard Hot 100 for eight weeks and reached the same position on the Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Singles & Tracks chart. It topped the Billboard Rhythmic chart and also peaked at number four on the Mainstream Top 40 ranking. The song was a radio hit in Canada, reaching number two on Radio & Records{{'}} CHR/Pop Top 30 chart. Outside North America, the song reached number one on the Eurochart Hot 100, topping the charts of Germany, the Netherlands, and the United Kingdom. Across the rest of Europe, the song became a top-five hit in several regions, including Flanders, France, Ireland, Norway, and Switzerland. In Australasia, "I Don't Wanna Know" peaked at number two in Australia and number three in New Zealand.

An answer to "I Don't Wanna Know" sung from a female perspective, "You Should Really Know", was released later the same year as Winans' single, on August 30, 2004. Created by producers the Pirates, it features Shola Ama, Naila Boss, and Ishani, and it uses the same Enya sample as the original. It also credits the writers of "You're a Customer", unlike the original. Although "You Should Really Know" did not achieve the level of success Winans' single did in the US, it was a top-10 hit in the United Kingdom, peaking at number eight on the UK Singles Chart, and it also reached the top 50 in Austria, the Czech Republic, France, Greece, and Ireland.

sections.heading: Charts
Others
sections.wikitext:
Later, another answer song called "I Already Know" sung by Noelle was released and had the same background melody as the original song. American R&B group [[Nina Sky]] also recorded their own version of their song entitled "Time to Go" featuring rapper [[Angie Martinez]]. The song has also been covered by Dega, a Kompa artist, featuring a rap verse from [[Wyclef Jean]] and a small section from [[T-Vice]] in the album ''Ba Li Gazzz'' in 2004.
{{Clear}}
